BiblicalUsage: Ahava is a river in Babylonia where Ezra gathers the returning exiles before the long journey home. The place is covered in the Biblical Places collection — this study covers only how the name is used.
TheologicalSignificance: A place name carries little theology on its own, and I will not pretend otherwise. What matters is what happened there: God's people stopped, fasted, and asked Him for safe passage instead of asking the king for soldiers.
RelatedTopics: Exile and Return; Prayer; God's Protection
